approach: Add `jobs::provenance(git, change, judged, history)` in crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs. It judges a job's records against cross-links that Athena's own writers always leave: request record, reader invocation, defaults hash, dispatch fields, brief file and its hash, and time order. It runs only in the live gate. `jobs::check` becomes `check_records` (the old body, unchanged) plus `provenance` when `history` is None. The history walk, the frozen legacy path and `check_after_cutover` are untouched, so D111 stays true. Every refusal is a `Rule::JobRecords` violation built by one local `fail(path, detail, repair)`; the detail starts with "provenance: " and names the missing or contradicting evidence, and the repair names the Athena command that writes it. R1 (any closing score or outcome of a request job, per reading): request.json exists with received_at <= reading.at; a Reader invocation with seq == invocation_seq ended at or before reading.at; if base_commit is held, defaults.toml at it hashes to defaults_sha256. R2 (Landed outcome only): job.json exists with the ten dispatch fields; its config and defaults hashes equal the accepted reading's; `<job dir>/brief-producer.md` is in the tree and its sha256 equals brief_sha256. R4 (Landed only, `dispatch_order_problem`): every non-reader invocation starts at or after dispatched_at; the verifier named by the verification starts at or after the latest lower-seq producer's end; outcome.at >= verifier.ended_at. Revision changes: (a) test (a) now builds the forgery acceptance review 2 describes (request, reading, reader invocation and a hand-written job.json in commit 1; code, candidate, verification, a verifier invocation copied from an earlier job and a Landed outcome in commit 2) and shows which rules refuse it, (brief-producer.md and 'before the job was dispatched'); the missing-request case is an extra variant. (b) `provenance` no longer calls `prediction_problem` and `dispatch_order_problem` no longer checks for a Verifier invocation, because `invariant::check` already runs both in the same gate scope; one fault gives one violation. (c) The docs and CHANGELOG say a (b) forgery written with current timestamps passes. (d) `check_pr_head` is named as the place to run provenance in CI without re-judging history, and the older-build close case is stated as a risk with a repair text and an open question. No record field is added.

decisions.choice: Wire the live gate through `jobs::check`: split into `check_records` (old body, unchanged) and `check`, which adds `provenance` when `history.is_none()`. Doc comments on `check` and `provenance`, and one at the `is_none()` branch, say `None` means a commit being made (lib.rs:357 and 372), `Some` is the frozen history walk (history.rs:255), and a future caller passing `None` on old commits gets provenance.
decisions.reason: The live gate gains the check and every history judgment (pre-C0, non-cutover walk, legacy.rs) stays byte-identical. No edit to lib.rs, legacy.rs, invariant.rs or history.rs. The tests pin both sides: the older-build non-cutover test and the gate wiring assertion in (c).

rejected.option: Call `jobs::provenance` from `gate()` in lib.rs
rejected.why: lib.rs is not a deliverable and the None/Some split reaches the same two sites.

rejected.option: Put the checks into `check_records` for every caller
rejected.why: Re-judges frozen pre-C0 records that older builds wrote without dispatch fields; the sha-keyed exempt list cannot grow after the fact.

rejected.option: Add a provenance flag to `invariant::HistoryState`
rejected.why: Edits invariant.rs for no gain over the None/Some split.

decisions.choice: Do not re-walk main's history for provenance (no c0..tip loop in `check_after_cutover`). Name the per-pull-request CI check, `check_pr_head` in crates/athena-core/src/pr_check.rs (run by `athena check --pr-head` in .github/workflows/ci.yml on every pull request), as the natural place for a follow-up that runs `jobs::provenance` in CI on a pull request's own commits only. It would catch a forger who commits with `--no-verify`, which the hook-only live gate misses.
decisions.reason: A loop over main since C0 reverses D111 item 7 (docs/decisions.md:2902-2907) and the comments at history.rs:36-37 and athena.toml:152, and judges every main commit that older builds wrote without provenance; the count cannot be measured because records/ is absent from the snapshot. A flagged commit already on main cannot be excused afterwards. `check_pr_head` sees only new commits, so those reasons do not apply to it, but pr_check.rs is in athena-core and is not a listed deliverable, and it classifies landing commits, not records-only commits such as the (c) close; adding records-only judgment there is a design change for the user to approve. The docs and CHANGELOG list the gap as a residual.

rejected.option: Keep the c0..tip loop and amend D111
rejected.why: Larger scope across non-deliverable docs and invariant.rs, with an unmeasured false-positive risk on this job's own CI.

rejected.option: Add pr_check.rs as a deliverable with a test there
rejected.why: Outside the listed deliverables, and it needs a decision on judging records-only commits in a pull request and on a remedy for a flagged one; offered as a follow-up (open question 1).

rejected.option: Walk provenance in the non-cutover history walk
rejected.why: Refuses genuine old jobs (dispatch fields are Options, records.rs:607-633) and squash-landed jobs whose base commit is gone, with no remedy.

decisions.choice: R1 applies to any closing of a request job, per reading; R2 and R4 apply only to a Landed outcome. Checked dispatch fields: accepted_reading, accepted_by, caps, base_commit, config_sha256, defaults_sha256, athena, driver, brief_sha256, dispatched_at. request_path, request_sha256, cost, tokens, note, pin and dispatch_branch are not required. The R1 refusal text for a missing reader invocation or request record says what it is and what to do: run `athena ask` for a new proposal; a reading from a build that did not write them cannot be closed here and is left for the owner (open question 2). The docs state this case.
decisions.reason: `athena close` of a Queued, Proposed or Declined job always commits a Score and an outcome through the live gate (manage.rs:103-115, 192), so R1 does reach it. A hand-made proposal closed this way is forgery (c), so R1 cannot be dropped for closes. Dispatch fields and the brief hash bind only a Landed outcome, so closing an interrupted or old-build dispatched job stays possible. Genuine dispatches write request_path, request_sha256, cost, tokens, note and pin as null (run/mod.rs:983-988). Whether any older-build reading lacks a reader invocation cannot be measured here (records/ absent), so it is a stated risk, not a claim.

rejected.option: Apply the reader-invocation link only when the invocation_seq names a non-Reader invocation
rejected.why: A hand-made proposal (c) has no reader invocation at all, so it would pass.

rejected.option: Require every dispatch field on every closing
rejected.why: Refuses genuine and old-build jobs.

rejected.option: Skip provenance when the commit declares an intervention
rejected.why: Gives a forger a one-line bypass, and the existing intervention rule is private to invariant.rs.

decisions.choice: Do not repeat rules the same gate scope already runs. `provenance` does not call `invariant::prediction_problem` (reading before dispatch and before non-reader invocations, invariant.rs:754, run at invariant.rs:638) and `dispatch_order_problem` does not check that the verification names a successful Verifier invocation (invariant.rs:713-723). `dispatch_order_problem` holds only the new orderings; when the verification names no verifier invocation, or the record is absent, it skips the verifier orderings, as `invariant::check` already refuses that. Its doc comment cites `prediction_problem` and the verifier-invocation check as the complement.
decisions.reason: `invariant::check` and `jobs::check` run side by side in the same scopes (lib.rs:356, 371), so one fault gave two violations; one violation is clearer for the owner. Reading-vs-dispatch order stays defined in one place. The cost is that `provenance_of` alone does not report a reading recorded after dispatch; that case is covered by the existing invariant tests and by an assertion through `crate::gate` in test (b).

rejected.option: Keep the `prediction_problem` call so `provenance_of` is complete on its own
rejected.why: Duplicates a refusal the same gate already makes; two wordings of one fact.

rejected.option: Re-implement reading-vs-dispatch order in R4
rejected.why: Duplicates prediction_problem with different wording.

rejected.option: Move R4 into invariant.rs
rejected.why: invariant.rs is not a deliverable.

decisions.choice: For a Landed outcome require `<job dir>/brief-producer.md` in the tree with sha256_hex equal to job.brief_sha256.
decisions.reason: The Dispatch commit writes brief_sha256 and the file together (run/mod.rs:981 and 994). A hand-written job.json must produce a consistent pair; the review's forger, who copies a hash or omits the brief, is refused ('brief-producer.md'). Cheap and exact.

rejected.option: Check brief_sha256 only for presence
rejected.why: Misses a job.json whose hash names no committed brief.

decisions.choice: A reading whose base_commit is not held is not refused; the defaults_sha256 recompute is skipped and the docs list this as a residual. The request record and reader invocation still gate every reading.
decisions.reason: A squash, gc, reset or shallow clone can drop the base, and the live gate has no remedy to offer. Only a held base lets defaults_sha256 be recomputed exactly (capability.rs:51).

rejected.option: Refuse an unheld base
rejected.why: False refusals with no remedy.

rejected.option: Recompute config_sha256 from athena.toml
rejected.why: It hashes `Config::reading_inputs()` (capability.rs:45), which follows the writing build's code; it is only compared between job.json and the reading.

decisions.choice: The verifier is ordered against the latest producer with a lower seq, not every producer. No producer is required.
decisions.reason: A retry makes a second producer start after the first verifier; a resumed kept candidate may have no producer record.

rejected.option: Verifier after every producer
rejected.why: Refuses genuine retry chains.

decisions.choice: Drop the rule 'job.json added before its reading is in the parent'.
decisions.reason: It refuses the genuine fixture `seed_accepted_jobs` (run/tests.rs:1413-1451), which commits Request, Reading and Job in one call, and a forger passes it with two commits. Forgery (a) is covered by R1 plus R2/R4 on a Landed outcome.

rejected.option: Keep it and edit the fixture
rejected.why: Edits a non-deliverable test file for a weak signal.

decisions.choice: State the limits of (a) and (b) plainly. (a) as acceptance review 2 built it (docs/design/reviews/athena-v0-acceptance-2.md:29-36) is refused when the hand-written job.json has no committed brief-producer.md or a hash that matches none, or when the verifier invocation copied from a real job started before dispatched_at; it passes when the forger also writes a matching brief file and consistent times. (b), a job dispatched and interrupted then closed by one forged commit, is caught only when its records contradict the dispatch: copied from another job, back-dated, or with a mismatched hash or field. A (b) forgery written with current timestamps falls after dispatched_at and keeps its order, so it passes. A control test records each limit. The docs and CHANGELOG say so.
decisions.reason: No committed value binds closing records to the dispatch that a forger cannot compute; signing is out of scope. Honest wording prevents the docs reading as stronger than the check.

rejected.option: Claim (b) is refused outright
rejected.why: Untrue for a forgery written with current times.

decisions.choice: Add no refusal_corpus case and leave records.rs, reconcile.rs and history.rs unedited though the brief lists them.
decisions.reason: The corpus (crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs) feeds request and reading text through the reading checkers; this plan adds no parser, stem list, stop list or reading check, and the input forms are record shapes mapped to landing_tests.rs tests. Every link used is already stored (Reading base_commit, defaults_sha256, invocation_seq, at; Request.received_at; Job dispatch fields; Invocation role, seq, started_at, ended_at), so no field or allow-list change is needed. A new witness field would be one a forger recomputes. The producer and verifier still run `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` as a no-regression command; I cite no case ids and no result.

rejected.option: Chain hash or witness field on Score or Outcome
rejected.why: Recomputable by the forger; real signing is out of scope.

rejected.option: Corpus cases for forged record shapes
rejected.why: The corpus runs request text, not commit records.

The lifecycle, job_plan and drain suites run real writers through the live gate. Step 6 treats a failure there as a bug in the check, never a reason to change the writer's records.

risks.risk: A genuine job dispatched by an older build lacks a required dispatch field or brief file and is refused when it lands after an upgrade; a proposal whose reading an older build wrote without a request record or reader invocation is refused when closed with `athena close` (manage.rs:103-115, 192). The live gate has no sha-keyed exempt remedy, and the count cannot be measured because records/ is absent.
risks.mitigation: Only a Landed outcome is held to dispatch fields and the brief hash, and the list is limited to the fields the rules use. Closes face R1 only. risks.risk: A base commit that is not held skips the defaults hash comparison, so a forger could name a bogus base.

demonstrations.method: Run the athena-gate suite. New tests in landing_tests.rs build real temporary git repositories and call `jobs::provenance` through a new helper `provenance_of(git, rev)`, and the live `crate::gate` for the wiring. They assert the Violation list. (a) `a_job_written_by_hand_across_two_commits_is_refused`, built as acceptance review 2 did: commit 1 holds request.json, a reading, a reader invocation and a hand-written job.json with all ten dispatch fields, with no brief-producer.md (variant 1) or with a brief_sha256 copied from another job and no matching file (variant 1b); `provenance_of` on commit 1 is empty because nothing closes. Commit 2 holds the hand change, candidate, verification, a verifier invocation whose times come from an earlier job (so before dispatched_at), and a Landed outcome. Assert violations whose detail contains 'brief-producer.md' and 'before the job was dispatched', each with a repair naming `athena go`. Variant 2 writes a brief file that matches job.json but keeps the copied verifier times: only 'before the job was dispatched' remains. Variant 3 (extra) omits the request record: detail contains 'no request record', repair contains 'athena ask'. Control `a_job_written_by_hand_with_every_link_consistent_still_passes`: matching brief and consistent times give no violation (recorded limit). (b) `a_forged_landing_of_a_dispatched_job_that_never_closed_is_refused`: a genuine Read commit (request, reading, reader invocation) and Dispatch commit (full job.json plus brief-producer.md), then one forged commit adding code and closing records copied or back-dated. Variants, each breaking one link: a producer started before dispatched_at; the verifier started before the producer ended; the outcome before the verifier ended; dispatched_at missing; the job's defaults hash differing from the reading's; brief-producer.md differing from brief_sha256. A reading recorded after dispatch is asserted through `crate::gate` (reported by the existing `prediction_problem`, not repeated by provenance). Control `..._written_with_current_times_still_passes` records that a forgery stamped with current times passes. (c) `a_hand_made_proposal_closed_with_athena_close_is_refused`: a reading with invented forecasts, no request record, no reader invocation, closed by a Score plus a Dropped outcome (the shape of manage.rs:195-207). Assert 'no request record' and 'no reader invocation'; the same commit through `crate::gate(git, &change, Scope::CommitMsg)` has a violation whose detail starts with 'provenance: '; a control with request, reader invocation, held base and matching defaults hash is accepted. (d) `the_older_build_job_in_a_non_cutover_history_is_not_refused`: an old-shape fixture with an unreachable base commit; `history_of(&git)` has no violation starting 'provenance: ', while `provenance_of` on its closing commit refuses. Existing genuine-landing tests still pass.
demonstrations.observes: Each forged history gives at least one Rule::JobRecords Violation with detail starting 'provenance: ' that names the evidence, and carries the commit. The controls, the genuine landing and the older-build history walk give none. All existing landing, chain, intervention and exemption tests pass, with `job_records_of` (landing_tests.rs:827) and jobs.rs `check_head` now calling `check_records`.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base code `jobs::check` never reads the request record, the reader invocation, the dispatch fields, the brief file and hash, defaults.toml at the base or the invocation times, so (a), (b) and (c) fail on `!violations.is_empty()` and the `detail.contains(..)` assertions; in (a) the 'brief-producer.md' and 'before the job was dispatched' assertions fail. Without the `history.is_none()` call in `check`, the Scope::CommitMsg assertion in (c) fails. If provenance ran in the plain history walk, (d) fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `crate::jobs::provenance` via a new helper `provenance_of(git, rev)` that builds `Change::of_commit` and `Judged::new` like the existing `job_records_of` (landing_tests.rs ~823-827); `crate::gate(.., Scope::CommitMsg)` (lib.rs:337); `crate::history::check_history` via the existing `history_of`. Fixtures are real temporary git repositories from `testutil::{repo, write, commit}` and `owner_repo` (exist). Plan step 5 adds `genuine_repo` (owner_repo plus a committed defaults.toml), `genuine_reading`, `genuine_job` (all dispatch fields, optional brief file and hash override), `request_record`, `copied_verifier` (an invocation record with earlier times) and `provenance_of`. Existing: `write_records`, `opening`, `closing`, `stage_landing`, `history_of`. Nothing in the gate is stubbed.

open_questions: User: Job records written only to the athena/records branch are not judged by this check, and neither main commits after C0 (D111 item 7 is kept) nor a pull request's own commits are judged for provenance in CI today. Should a follow-up job run `jobs::provenance` inside `check_pr_head` (crates/athena-core/src/pr_check.rs), over the pull request's own commits only and including records-only commits, so a commit made with `--no-verify` is caught without re-walking main? I recommend yes for `check_pr_head`, and a layout adapter for athena/records only after the false-positive rate can be measured.

User: A reading written by a build that did not record a request record or a reader invocation cannot pass R1 when its job is closed with `athena close`, and the live gate has no exempt list to excuse it. Records/ is absent from this snapshot, so the number of such jobs cannot be measured here. Should a follow-up add a remedy (for example an owner-declared intervention that excuses R1 for one named job), or is closing such jobs by another route acceptable?
